label: PF Backlog 639
title: Grooming hook: auto-attach design guardrails during grooming (zero-touch)
body: Follow-up to BI-PF-1467. The design guardrails exist as a CLI and in the design review prompt, but nothing forces them onto an item when it is groomed. Add a core grooming hook so every groomed spec is produced against the guardrails and the item records that they were applied, with no manual step.

objective: Grooming hook: auto-attach design guardrails during grooming (zero-touch)
acceptance_criteria: The AI grooming prompt for a single item includes the DESIGN GUARDRAILS block (checklist, relevant corrections, recurring findings) so the produced spec addresses them.
The batched AI grooming prompt (groom_all) also includes a DESIGN GUARDRAILS block covering the batched items, so batch grooming is not weaker than single grooming.
Every groom path (groom, groom_all, regroom) appends an idempotent 'Design guardrails applied (<id>): sig:<digest>' marker to the item evidence without creating a new store or API route.
The guardrails logic has a single owner in core (core/design_guardrails.py); the existing scripts/dev CLI delegates to it and its tests keep passing.
A deterministic test proves the grooming prompt contains DESIGN GUARDRAILS and that a deterministic groom records the marker exactly once on re-groom.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/grooming.py to invoke core/guardrails.py + core/design_critic.py at groom time; stamp an applied_guardrails block (guardrail set, version, hash) onto the groomed spec; expose via existing /api/v1/backlog/grooming/guidelines endpoint and config/grooming-guidelines.json; reuse core/design_tokens.py for guardrail rendering.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1467 guardrails to exist (state: implemented)
RELATED BI-PF-1258 restamp/regroom must re-apply guardrails
RELATED BI-PF-1250 epic-grooming hook shares core/grooming.py
conflict_findings: BI-PF-1258 also modifies core/grooming.py restamp path
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1467 defines guardrail content; this only automates attachment
analysis.rationale: Grooming pipeline and guardrail engine both exist; this item is a small wiring+stamping change, not new capability.
assumptions: BI-PF-1467 shipped a stable guardrails CLI/API
Grooming hook ordering: guardrails after parse, before spec finalization
Guardrail application is deterministic given config hash
risks: Guardrail evaluation cost on large specs
Guardrail version churn causing spurious restamps
Bikeshed on which guardrail set applies per item type
evidence: Candidate code shows core/guardrails.py + core/design_critic.py already exist
missing_info: Which guardrail sets map to which item types/epics
Whether guardrail failure blocks grooming or only annotates
Restamp cadence when guardrail config changes

context_review.reason: Acceptance criteria are concrete: they name the single owner module (core/design_guardrails.py), the exact paths to hook (groom, groom_all, regroom), the required DESIGN GUARDRAILS prompt block, the idempotent evidence marker format, the constraint to avoid new stores/routes, delegation from scripts/dev CLI, and the deterministic test to add. WHY is well-stated (guardrails exist but aren't enforced at grooming, zero-touch requirement). These are enough for a standalone engineer/agent to implement without further digging, even though the APPROACH and AFFECTED_* fields are boilerplate.

api_impact.reason: internal grooming/worker hook: no external API surface; reuses existing backlog context writes.
